The Sean Ellis test asks users how disappointed they would be if they could no longer use a product. If at least 40% say “very disappointed,” that is a strong signal of product-market fit—not definitive proof. [S3] [S5] [S6] [S7]

## How it works

Ask users: “How would you feel if you could no longer use this product?” Offer the choices “very disappointed,” “somewhat disappointed,” “not disappointed,” or “not applicable—I’ve already stopped using the product.” The commonly cited benchmark is at least 40% choosing “very disappointed.”

[S3] [S5]

## How to interpret it

The result helps identify whether users consider the product a must-have. Ellis describes it as a useful signal, including for an early MVP, but says retention is the ultimate test; reaching 40% alone does not guarantee success.
